articles.title: Give an interface room to breathe
articles.author: NNT Lab
articles.excerpt: Spacing is a way to show relationships, not simply a decorative margin.
body: Start with the task a person came to complete. Place the title, supporting information, and primary action close enough to read as a group. Separate groups with more space than the space within each group.
A small spacing scale keeps the page coherent. Try 4, 8, 16, 24, 40, and 64 pixels. Choose a level because of the relationship it communicates, then check the result on a narrow screen.
White space cannot repair missing information. Label fields clearly, show useful validation next to the input, and keep the next step visible. A quiet interface should still explain itself.

articles.title: A browser request has a whole journey
articles.author: NNT Lab
articles.excerpt: Follow a form submission from the screen to a durable database row.
body: A button click can create a request, but the server decides what is allowed. The browser sends a small JSON body, the server validates its types and limits, and the database stores the accepted record.

Never trust a product price submitted by the browser. Send a product identifier and quantity. The server retrieves its own price and calculates the total. The interface then displays the returned result.

A useful test follows this entire path. Submit a form through HTTP, read the result back, restart the server, and confirm that the record still exists. This checks behavior that a static screenshot cannot show.

articles.title: Start an analysis with a question
articles.author: NNT Lab
articles.excerpt: A precise question makes the chart, aggregation, and caveats easier to choose.
body: Which decision will this analysis support? A question such as “which channel grew last month?” is more useful than “show all the data.” It tells you the measure, grouping, and time window.
Inspect missing values and units before calculating. If one source reports baht and another reports satang, a clean-looking chart can still be wrong by a factor of one hundred.

Write down the important limitations next to the result. A change in recorded sales may reflect a change in collection, stock availability, or customer behavior. An honest chart helps the reader tell these possibilities apart.

articles.title: A model needs a baseline and a boundary
articles.author: NNT Lab
articles.excerpt: A small model with clear evaluation can teach more than a large unsupported claim.
body: Choose a baseline before training. For a classifier, predicting the most common class is a useful first comparison. For a forecast, the previous period or a moving average may already be strong.

Keep evaluation examples separate from training. Tune thresholds on a development split and report final results on held-out examples. A score on a tiny synthetic set is educational evidence, not a production guarantee.

Allow the system to say it is uncertain. This lab uses character-pattern coverage and the leading model score to flag weak inputs. Its Naive Bayes scores are uncalibrated and should not be presented as the probability that an answer is correct.

articles.title: Useful interactions welcome more people
articles.author: NNT Lab
articles.excerpt: Keyboard focus, labels, and readable feedback improve the everyday experience.
body: Use a real button for an action and an anchor for navigation. Native elements already understand keyboard input and expose meaning to assistive technology.
Every input needs an associated visible label. Placeholder text disappears when typing and cannot replace a label. Errors should explain how to fix the input without relying on color alone.

Check the flow with a keyboard. Focus should stay visible, dialogs should be escapable, and a successful submission should announce a clear status. Reduced-motion preferences should also be respected.

articles.title: Show the decisions behind the result
articles.author: NNT Lab
articles.excerpt: A strong project page explains what works, how you know, and what remains.
body: Introduce a project with the problem and the person it helps. Follow with a live demonstration, a concise architecture explanation, and the most useful screenshot.

Show real evidence: API tests, a reproducible setup, example data, and a list of limitations. If an integration is simulated or a model uses synthetic examples, say so in the interface and the README.

During an interview, walk through one request and one tradeoff. Explain why the server owns prices, why records are scoped to a workspace, or how you selected an uncertainty threshold. Understanding your own work is more valuable than listing many technologies.

courses.title: From browser to database
courses.description: Understand the request journey through this very project.

lessons.title: Validate at the boundary
lessons.body: Browser validation improves feedback, but clients can be modified. A server must validate JSON types, length limits, integer ranges, allowed values, and entity identifiers before storing data. Parameterized SQL keeps input separate from the SQL statement.
lessons.question: Where must validation happen before data is stored?
choices: On the server, even if the browser also validates

lessons.title: Persist the accepted result
lessons.body: A server-side SQLite transaction makes related updates atomic. This lab stores records in a local database, associates each with an anonymous workspace, and checks workspace ownership when reading, updating, or deleting. Restarting the server keeps the records when the same database file is used.
lessons.question: What makes a saved record survive a server restart?
choices: Keeping it in a JavaScript array
Writing it to a durable database file

lessons.title: Protect a browser write
lessons.body: A session cookie identifies the workspace. HttpOnly prevents page scripts from reading the cookie. A CSRF token and same-origin checks protect browser writes against cross-site requests. These demo workspaces are not user accounts and do not replace authentication in a production app.
lessons.question: Which combination protects this demo’s browser writes?
choices: A CSRF token and same-origin checks

courses.title: Useful data stories
courses.description: Choose a measure, check its units, and communicate honestly.

lessons.title: Respect the unit
lessons.body: All monetary values in this API are integer satang: one baht equals 100 satang. Integer arithmetic avoids many floating-point rounding surprises. Sum the integer values first, then format them for display in baht. Record currency and time zone when combining data sources.
lessons.question: How many satang does the API store for ฿12.50?

lessons.title: Choose an honest comparison
lessons.body: Compare the same metric over comparable time windows. A total over 31 days may be larger than a total over 28 days without any improvement per day. Consider showing both totals and a normalized rate, and explain missing data or changes in collection.
lessons.question: What can make a monthly comparison misleading?

lessons.title: Make a chart readable
lessons.body: A bar chart usually needs a zero baseline because its lengths encode quantities. Label axes and units, show the relevant period, and use color consistently. Include the underlying numbers or an export so people can inspect the evidence behind the visual.
lessons.question: Why do bars usually need a zero baseline?

courses.title: Apply a small model responsibly
courses.description: Learn what the local text classifier can and cannot tell you.

lessons.title: Separate training and evaluation
lessons.body: The local support classifier is a character n-gram Multinomial Naive Bayes model trained on educational synthetic Thai and English messages. To assess a model, keep evaluation examples out of training. A model that memorizes training data may still fail on unseen messages.
lessons.question: Which examples should be excluded from training?

lessons.title: Read scores carefully
lessons.body: Naive Bayes combines learned feature likelihoods and class priors. Its normalized class scores are not calibrated probabilities of correctness. Familiar character patterns may produce a strong score even when a message is outside the intended support-ticket domain.
lessons.question: A model score of 0.95 means what in this demo?
choices: A guaranteed 95% chance of being correct
An uncalibrated model score, not a correctness probability

lessons.title: Make uncertainty visible
lessons.body: The classifier marks a prediction uncertain when familiar-pattern coverage or the leading score falls below a development threshold. An abstention is a signal to review the input rather than blindly accept the top label. Thresholds must be re-evaluated with realistic data before production use.
lessons.question: What should an uncertain result encourage?
choices: Human review or a clearer input
Treating the top label as certain
